name: Arankale Bannaggama Bana Maduwa
description: Arankale Bannaggama Bana Maduwa is a remarkable preachers' hall located in Kurunagala, North Western Province, Sri Lanka. Dating back to ancient times, this historical site offers a glimpse into the religious and cultural practices of Sri Lanka during the Anuradhapura era. The Bana Maduwa, or preaching hall, served as a place where Buddhist monks would deliver sermons and educate the local populace about the teachings of Buddhism. Visitors can explore the well-preserved ruins, which include stone walls and pillars, showcasing the architectural style of the period. The site also provides a serene atmosphere for meditation and reflection. Guided tours are available, providing insights into the history and significance of the location. While the exact dates of its construction are unknown, it is believed to have been built between the 3rd century BCE and the 1st century CE. The Bana Maduwa is not only a testament to the past but also a symbol of the rich cultural heritage of Sri Lanka, making it a must-visit for those interested in history and religion.
activities: Guided tours, Photography, Meditation

Visitors can explore the ruins and learn about the rich history and cultural significance of the area.
